## The problem

::: {layout="[58,42]" layout-valign="center"}
::: {}
Batoukop's health centre had beds but almost nothing else. Consultation and delivery rooms were **empty, scantily furnished and under-resourced**. Residents had to travel to get even basic diagnostic tests.

As a result, the community had **no systematic data on its own disease burden**.
:::

![A consultation and delivery room before the project: a single bed and drip stand in a bare room.](images/batoukop/room-before.jpg){.photo fig-alt="A small bare room with concrete walls, a single metal bed with a blue mattress and an IV drip stand, lit by one bulb."}
:::

## Equipping the clinic

I secured about **$1,000** and spent it on the essentials for a working diagnostic bench: a binocular **microscope**, a **centrifuge**, a **haemoglobin analyser**, **Widal slide test kits**, blood collection tubes, slides, immersion oil, reagents and gloves.

![The supplies, set up and ready for use.](images/batoukop/supplies.jpg){.photo fig-alt="A wooden table holding a microscope, a centrifuge, racks of blood collection tubes, a URIT-12 haemoglobin analyser, a Rapid Widal test kit, boxes of gloves and bottles of reagents."}

::: {.gallery layout-ncol=3}
![Unpacking the equipment in the clinic's waiting area.](images/batoukop/unpacking.jpg){.photo fig-alt="Two people unpack a centrifuge from a cardboard box on the floor of a clinic waiting room, beside boxes of supplies and racks of tubes."}

![Handing the microscope over to the clinic director.](images/batoukop/handover.jpg){.photo fig-alt="Ronald, in a Mastercard Foundation and USIU-Africa t-shirt, stands beside the clinic director in a white coat, who holds up the new microscope."}

![A thank-you from the clinic director.](images/batoukop/thanks.jpg){.photo fig-alt="The clinic director, smiling, hugs Ronald after receiving the equipment."}
:::

## The open clinic

::: {layout="[58,42]" layout-valign="center"}
::: {}
With the equipment in place, I designed and ran a **one-month free testing clinic**. Community members came in for blood sampling and on-site testing for **malaria**, **typhoid (Widal)** and **anemia**.

I then analysed the results to produce the community's first baseline prevalence figures and recommended **clinical follow-up and referral pathways** for people who needed further care.
:::

![Collecting a blood sample during the open clinic. The participant's face is blurred for privacy.](images/batoukop/open-clinic.jpg){.photo fig-alt="A health worker in a white coat and gloves draws blood from the arm of a seated woman whose face is blurred."}
:::

## Findings

::: {.stats}
::: {.stat}
[58%]{.num}
[malaria positivity]{.label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[71%]{.num}
[Widal test positivity]{.label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[28%]{.num}
[mild anemia]{.label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[5%]{.num}
[severe anemia]{.label}
:::
:::

These are the community's **first systematic baseline prevalence figures**. The anemia burden in particular led to recommendations for clinical follow-up and referral.
